follow-on: the machine-map landed record still names SshTransport as a public symbol at lines 231 and 696; after this rename the public class is SubprocessTransport. The file is outside this node's write scope, so it is recorded rather than edited.

item_verdicts.diff: empty ssh_command makes _argv() return a local nice -n 19 python -c REMOTE_SCRIPT list and leaves the ssh branch unchanged; SshTransport is renamed SubprocessTransport with both callers and __all__ moved, no new Transport class; a 206-line test drives the local route end to end through a stand-in wrapper.
item_verdicts.done_when: a stand-in eddb_pwrapper on the script's path returns E101154 pf_active arrays; the local transport returns records whose data and time arrays equal the stand-in bit for bit, decoded by the shared decode_batch. Gate 35 passed EXIT=0 independently reproduced in an extracted tree at d2f678e4.
item_verdicts.goal: the node goal is to let the EDDB reader run locally with no ssh hop on the analysis server; with an empty ssh_command _argv() composes nice -n 19 <remote_python> -c REMOTE_SCRIPT as one argv list and the ssh route keeps its module-load string, exactly as the plan paragraph names.
item_verdicts.manifest: records commit d2f678e4, both arms, the negative control and the clean-venv gate with log paths, and no blockers; its baseline_suite/after_suite JSON agree with the cited logs.
item_verdicts.verification: the head gate, the base arm and a mutation of the guard were all re-run independently from a git-archive extraction of d2f678e4 under $TMPDIR, not from the worker's logs alone.
item_verdicts.write_paths: git show --name-only d2f678e4 lists the fragment, eddb_remote.py, test_eddb_local_transport.py and tests/data/test_eddb_cache.py, all inside the fence; eddb.py and the figures dir are declared but untouched.

justifications.durability: three local-route tests are added and the negative control proves they fire when the local branch is disabled; the cached pf_active test is not skipped (the store exists and 35 passed carry no skip marker), so the bit-for-bit claim is exercised rather than short-circuited.
justifications.evidence: local-tests.log records 35 passed EXIT=0 at d2f678e4 and I reproduced it in an extracted tree; base-arm.log records 32 passed EXIT=0 at 0a77985f; negative-control.log shows 3 failed EXIT=1 and my own mutation of `if not self.ssh_command:` to `if False:` reproduced the same 3 failures; ruff exit 0. Blemish: the clean-venv gate header names revision 0a77985f though its installed wheel matches head.
justifications.fit: the rename keeps the Transport protocol and the runner's shape, docstrings and the module header are updated to the two-route reality, the commit carries a conventional subject and a mechanism body, and the fragment element id begins with the node id.
justifications.goal_fidelity: plan jt60sa-facility-mint §3 names exactly this: an empty ssh_command composes nice -n 19 <python> -c REMOTE_SCRIPT with no ssh prefix and no module shell, the module-load string stays only on the ssh route, SshTransport is renamed and every caller moves, no new Transport class, and one shared reader and decode_batch. The diff matches clause for clause.
justifications.reuse: no abstraction is added; the local route reuses the same REMOTE_SCRIPT, encode_batch/decode_batch and SubprocessTransport that the ssh route uses, and the test's stand-in is a local fixture rather than a product change.
justifications.scope_discipline: only the four declared paths are touched; eddb.py, the figures dir, the plan and all index/sprint state are untouched; changed_paths match the diff.
